markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (100%)** · Confident · Read in turn
Only Invasive remains in the 90% conformal set [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 100%, InSitu 0% | One class dominates |
| Conformal set | {Invasive} | Single class at 90% |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.99 / 26th percentile | Typical, unflagged input |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Independent model concurs |
| Similar cases | 5 of 5 Invasive [F5] | Neighbors fully concordant |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 0, 8, 9) · ↑ invasive · Strongest concept association; above typical here [F2] · Validated
- **Tumor cell burden** (regions 1, 2, 6) · context · 69% neoplastic nuclei; density at 97th percentile [F7, F8] · Measured
- **Nuclear size** (regions 1, 2, 6) · context · Mean area lowest in reference; size variation highest [F9, F10] · Measured
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (regions 4, 7, 9) · context · Concept model links it to lower invasive likelihood [F3] · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0 (−0.005 to 0.007), so concepts are not shown to reflect the classifier. Mitoses (0/20) is unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Unsampled regions differ: cell metrics cover only 3 of 12 regions.
- Calibration is off: ECE 5% (CI 3–18%) on 132 test images.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 0, 8, 9:** Confirm tumor cells infiltrate stroma rather than staying within ducts.
2. **Regions 1, 2, 6:** Verify tumor nuclei, measured small and variable in size; count mitoses directly.
3. **Regions 4, 7, 9:** Judge whether the lymphocytic infiltrate is genuine TILs near tumor.
